title: Roman road cross-section sheet
subject: History
unit: Summer 1: The Roman Empire and Roman Britain (Flow)
source: Seeded from history/y3 lesson 16 (Roman road cross-section sheet (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 16: Roman roads, aqueducts and baths. To understand how Roman engineering changed Britain

model.title: How does water reach the town?

parts.label: Step 1
parts.text: Start at a spring high in the hills

parts.label: Step 2
parts.text: Build a channel sloping gently down

parts.label: Step 4
parts.text: Water flows downhill into the town

parts.label: Answer
parts.text: Gravity pulls the water along the slope

questions.q: Why did Roman roads have ditches?
questions.a: To carry rain away so the road stayed dry
questions.model: Rain falls on the road. The curved top makes it run to the sides. The ditches carry it away.

questions.q: Name a Roman road in Britain.
questions.a: Watling Street, the Fosse Way or Ermine Street

questions.q: What is the Roman name for Bath?
Draw and label a cross-section of a Roman road (4 layers and ditches), then write what each part is for.
questions.model: Teacher draws the bottom layer of big stones first.

questions.q: Explain in two sentences how an aqueduct works.
questions.a: It carries water from a high spring along a gentle downhill slope. Gravity pulls the water into the town.

questions.q: Which Roman invention do we still use most today? Why?
questions.a: For example: roads, because we still travel and trade

questions.q: Big question: why are some roads still straight?
questions.a: Roman engineers built them straight, and later roads followed the same routes
